sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks C15 row 14; Internal Quality Checks C15 row 14 annotations: 'If task data itself contain credential flag it. Only in toml we allow.')
evidence: The only shipped data file is environment/assets/seed_data.json (5903 bytes; byte-identical to solution/app/seed/seed_data.json, sha256 b256f85e58dde8370cd3577123f785daf6988f4d00506533f19485279dca7bf8); it parses as JSON. A scripted integrity pass (python -B -I) found zero problems: 18 unique message ids K-1..K-18; every matter.client is a client-role account; walled list contains only staff (dev on M-12); every author exists and is either staff not walled from the matter or that matter's own client; timer_days values (7, null, 30) are in timer_options_days [null,1,7,30]; every parent (K-14->K-1, K-15->K-14, K-4->K-3, K-12->K-6, K-9->K-8) resolves within the same matter and predates its reply; all timestamps are <= clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z and in order per matter; version timestamps do not postdate messages; every read_up_to marker names an existing message in the named matter and only for users who can see that matter (no dev/M-12, no Gwen/M-12, Paul only M-12). Accounts/roles match walls-and-retention.md:58-68 and tests/app_context.md:10-16. Two messages expire at import (K-1 on a 7-day matter, K-10 exactly 7 days old) - these are deliberate, publicly documented fixtures (walls-and-retention.md:76-78: 'a message sent exactly seven days ago ... is already gone'; replies to a deleted message stay with a deleted placeholder), and no read marker points to an expiring message, so they are not orphan defects. People use common names with RFC 2606 reserved kittle.test addresses; no phone, address, DOB, real company identifiers, passwords, tokens or keys in the seed (grep for password/secret/api key/token/script/onerror/javascript:/'ignore previous' returned nothing). The demo password password123 lives only in the brief notes and app_context, which the profile/internal annotation permit. Free text contains no prompt-injection; K-16 ('Schedule 2 ... rent') and K-12 ('*Schedule 4*') are benign formatting fixtures matching conversations.md:22's escaping/formatting requirement. Adversarial angle: no criterion depends on seed message text or ids (tests prompts reference only M-ids/accounts and state 'do not assume the seed state'), so a conforming app cannot be failed by a seed inconsistency, and the seed cannot let a broken app pass.
